requirement:
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |

Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
I judged the tests adequate. I did not read the implementation. All four tests carry a {test} reference to `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.items`.

Obligations and the tests that cover them:

1. **Block and flow mapping entries are `pair` items named by the written key.**
   - `toml_and_yaml_profiles_name_keys` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs`) checks block pairs `pair[a]` and `pair["b"]`. The quoted key keeps its quotes.
   - The same test checks the flow-mapping pair `pair["b"]/pair[c]/pair[d]`.
   - `yaml_selectors_encode_written_keys_and_number_duplicate_siblings` (`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs`) checks keys containing a space and special characters. It also checks duplicate block keys and duplicate keys inside a flow mapping.

2. **Block sequence entries are anonymous `item` items.** The first test asserts `item@` entries for both a mapping entry (`- f: 1`) and a scalar entry (`- 2`).

3. **Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.**
   - The first test asserts the selector hierarchy: pair under pair, pair under flow pair, item under pair, and pair under item.
   - The outline_content test also asserts nested selectors such as `pair[my%20key]/pair[...]`.

4. **The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends to include owned comments.**
   - The first test asserts exact line ranges, for example `pair[a] 1-2`. The leading `# c` comment is included, and the nested spans end at their last token.
   - `yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry` asserts that a same-line trailing comment is included in the selected text.
   - The same test asserts that the comment before `d` is part of `pair[d]` and is excluded from `pair[a]`. That shows `pair[a]` ends at its last non-comment token, `b: 1`.
   - It also asserts that the root item span equals the selected text span.

5. **Comment ownership follows `requirements.references.outline_comments`.** This requirement only cites the rule, and its own tests are not reassessed here. The YAML-specific application is covered by `yaml_comments_before_a_key_belong_to_that_key_not_the_previous_one`. A comment before `second` belongs to `pair[jobs]/pair[second]`, not to the preceding sibling's deeper nesting.

6. **Selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate suffixes follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.** The outline_content test asserts percent-encoding (`my%20key`, `a%2Fb%23c%40d%5Be%5D`) and `#1`/`#2` suffixes for duplicate pairs. The first test asserts the anonymous `item@` identity.

I found no required scenario that the tests miss. Item-in-item nesting and spans of items that own comments are not exercised separately. They follow the same nesting and comment-ownership mechanism that the tests above check for pairs, and the text does not distinguish them.

text: :::{req} items
The YAML outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:
| Construct | Kind | Name |
| Block and flow mapping entries | `pair` | Written key |
| Block sequence entries | `item` | Anonymous |
Nested entries appear beneath their nearest enclosing outline item.
The span covers the entry through its last non-comment token and extends
to include its owned comments. Comment ownership follows
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph remains ordinary paragraph text. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. Habeas MUST retain the
one-based line and UTF-8 byte column of each inline role’s opening brace or
fenced reference’s first opening colon. When siblings share a line, the
reference belongs to the item owning the comment at that position. A reference
in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.tests` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} outline_selectors
Habeas uses the TBV [outline selector grammar](sdk/outlines.md#parse-an-outline-selector)
under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` for source addresses.
